text:
harry: quick summary from today's onboarding: multiple teams hit surprising hangs with Generator.Stream when they rely solely on ctx cancellation. users expect immediate teardown but internal handshake retries can keep resources alive.

harry: i sketched a small ergonomic surface that preserves range-style usage but gives a clear escape hatch for callers who need deterministic teardown. idea: introduce an Iterator object with Read()/Abort()/DoneCtx() and keep a convenience Range() helper.

harry: proposed minimal shape:
```go
type Iterator interface {
  // Read blocks until the next token or returns io.EOF when the stream finishes.
  Read(ctx context.Context) (Token, error)
  // Abort force-closes the stream and releases any underlying transport / handshake goroutines.
  Abort() error
  // DoneCtx returns a read-only context canceled when the iterator is aborted or naturally completed.
  DoneCtx() context.Context
}

// convenience for folks who like range loops
func Range(ctx context.Context, it Iterator) <-chan Token
```

anya: +1. Abort() is great because callers in HTTP handlers or CLI tools can call it on early exit. DoneCtx() also helps background workers watching stream lifecycle.

chris: implementation notes: make internal handshakes derive from it.DoneCtx() (not caller ctx) so Abort() cancels mid-handshake. Also ensure Abort closes any idle net.Conn so blocked dials wake up. Abort must be idempotent.

tess: can we keep backwards compat by making Stream(...) return the old channel by default and adding a new StreamIterator(...) API? then docs recommend the iterator for robust apps.

harry: yep that's the plan. StreamIterator(...) returns Iterator; Stream(ctx, ...) remains but is implemented with Range(ctx, it) to avoid duplicated logic. deprecate ChannelStream in one major release.

anya: test plan: handshake-abort-no-leak, abort-idempotency-race, channel-shim-parity. add a fake auth server that returns 401 mid-handshake and a token rotator to exercise retries. assert goroutine count stable across many start/abort cycles.

chris: add metric active_iterators_total (labels: client, model). support folks asked for this so they can triage stuck streams without debugging goroutine dumps. guard any debug endpoint behind an env flag.

tess: DX note: update the Go quickstart and sampleapps to always show defer it.Abort() when iterator is used in short-lived contexts. also add a short migration snippet from channel->Iterator with Range() shim.

harry: i'll open a draft PR with the iterator, channel shim, tests, sampleapp edits, and docs. assigning to @chris for runtime review and @tess for docs + sampleapps. will include a small stress runner under samples/stream_aborts.

devex-bot: created draft PR harry/iterator-abort-api (WIP) — CI queued

anya: +1 to adding DoneCtx() to the API. small nit: call it ContextDone() or LifetimeCtx() to avoid confusion with caller contexts? not a blocker.

chris: LifetimeCtx() reads nicer. also add a note in README about how Resume()/background workers should use it for coordinated shutdown instead of relying on global cancellations.

harry: good call — i'll name it LifetimeCtx() in the PR and add the README section with examples for Resume and auth-rotation coordination. will ping sampleapps when draft is ready. :rocket:
